name: Nori Robotics

team.summary: Founder Antonio started working on Nori while doing robotics research at Columbia, teaching robots through human demonstrations.

product.summary: A $1,688 bimanual mobile robot with 19 degrees of freedom, designed for robotics developers and researchers.

market.summary: Robotics developers, researchers, and hobbyists looking for affordable hardware to collect datasets and test applications.

risks.risk: Hardware reliability, durability, and limitations of RC-style servos leading to jerky motion and lack of precision.
Sustainability of a low-cost hardware business model, referenced against similar failed ventures like K-scale labs.
Scepticism regarding marketing claims versus actual autonomous capabilities in unstructured real-world environments.

founder_depth.why: Founder has robotics research background at Columbia, but lacks prior commercial shipping or exit history mentioned.

shipping_evidence.why: The team has built seven iterations, shipped the first robot, published an academic paper, and provided an SDK and simulator.

demand_signal.why: Strong HN engagement with 201 points and 66 comments showing developer and hobbyist interest, though no revenue figures or named enterprise customers provided.

defensibility.why: Low-cost hardware using off-the-shelf components and RC-style servos with portions open-sourced, facing significant competition in a hardware race to the bottom.

analysis.thesis_fit_reason: Nori Robotics builds physical humanoid robot hardware, which is explicitly out of scope as a physical product.
analysis.case_summary: Strong developer interest and impressive price point for a bimanual robot, but disqualified by the thesis due to being a physical hardware product.
would_change_my_mind: Revising the thesis to include physical hardware and robotics devices.
Transitioning the business model entirely to pure AI software/infra for robotics control without hardware sales.
data_gaps: Exact revenue metrics and production volume numbers
Detailed enterprise or institutional customer list
